run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T08:42:05Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is being fed by a low, steady stream of error spans on the proxy's inbound operation "ingress" (SPAN_KIND_SERVER). Every observed one of those failures is an HTTP 503 logged by the frontend-proxy Envoy pod as "UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}" against its upstream frontend, i.e. the frontend terminated the connection before sending a response. The frontend pod itself is Ready, has 0 restarts, produced no error spans of its own, and shows stable CPU/memory, so no frontend application failure is visible; the exact reason the frontend resets those pooled connections is not established because Jaeger returned no traces for the window and the frontend container emitted no readable log lines. The error rate is not a new deviation: the proxy's error-span counter rose at ~0.8-1 span/min throughout 08:15-08:49 (about 0.07% of ~1,300 ingress spans/min) and was already at 557 when first observed at 08:15:00, ~13 min after the 08:02 rollout. A NetworkPolicy named frontend-block-all-ports appeared at 08:36:13, six minutes before the alert, but its spec is a single empty (allow-all) ingress rule and neither traffic volume nor error rate changed after it was created, so it is rejected as the cause. A fraud-detection OOMKill at 08:07:34 is a separate, recovered event on a different call path. Root cause is not established; the alert condition (">0") is being met by a persistent low-level 503 trickle from the frontend upstream.

claims.text: All STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans attributed to service frontend-proxy are on operation "ingress" with span_kind SPAN_KIND_SERVER; operation "router frontend egress" has zero error spans. frontend-proxy exposes only these two span operations.

Envoy access logs of pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-p6mgt (08:29-08:35) interleave successful "200 - via_upstream" lines with HTTP 503 lines carrying flag "UC" and message "upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}" for requests such as "GET /", "GET /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N" and "GET /api/recommendations?productIds=2ZYFJ3GM2N"; the access-log lines identify the upstream as "frontend".

Service frontend in otel-demo is ClusterIP 100.70.94.93:8080 with selector opentelemetry.io/name=frontend and exactly one endpoint, 100.96.2.139, targeting pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh; so the proxy's "frontend" upstream is that single frontend pod.

Service frontend itself reported no error spans in the window: STATUS_CODE_ERROR was 0 for frontend in the per-service status breakdown, and the 2-minute per-operation error breakdown shows only zeros for frontend operations including GET, POST, executing api route (pages) /api/data, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and tcp.connect.

Pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh is Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and no previous terminated container instance; it is owned by ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5 (created 08:02:10) owned by Deployment frontend, and Deployment frontend shows 1/1 available/ready/updated at generation 1, created 2026-11-17T08:02:08Z.

Frontend container CPU was ~0.048-0.053 cores against a 100m limit with a CFS throttled-period ratio of 0.26-0.37; frontend-proxy used ~0.0134-0.0141 cores against a 30m limit with a throttled ratio of 0.048-0.072; container_memory_failcnt was 0 for every pod in otel-demo, including frontend, across the window.

The frontend container's memory working set was 246,169,600 bytes at 08:15:00 and 257,490,944 bytes at 08:48 (about 235-246 MiB) while the pod spec declares a 200Mi memory limit, yet no OOMKilled termination or restart was recorded for that container.

The frontend-proxy ingress error counter rose only in small steps across the window: 557 error spans against 7,091 ingress spans at 08:15:00, 561 at 08:19:27, 578 at 08:32:27 and 588 at 08:49:27 (increments of 0-3 per minute), while the ingress request rate was ~1,244-1,462 spans/min from 08:31 to 08:47.

The span-metric counter is produced by pod otel-collector-564d9c7987-6j4x2, which started at 08:02:12, and the earliest metric samples available in this Prometheus are at 08:15:00/08:15:05 (Prometheus container started 08:11:32); therefore the 557 error spans already present at 08:15:00 accrued within roughly 13 minutes of the 08:02:12 collector start.

The only NetworkPolicy in the cluster is otel-demo/frontend-block-all-ports, created 2026-11-17T08:36:13Z, whose podSelector matches labels app.kubernetes.io/component=frontend, app.kubernetes.io/name=frontend and opentelemetry.io/name=frontend, with policyTypes [Ingress] and spec.ingress = [{}] (a single rule with no from and no ports).

After the NetworkPolicy was created at 08:36:13, traffic through the proxy did not change (1,244-1,462 ingress spans/min continued) and the frontend-proxy error counter kept its same pace (578 at 08:32:27 to 588 at 08:49:27, ~0.8-1/min).

flagd-config ConfigMap demo.flagd.json declares every fault-injection flag with defaultVariant "off" (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure).

Pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-wvrwx had one restart whose last termination was OOMKilled with exitCode 137 finishedAt 2026-11-17T08:07:34Z; the current instance started 08:07:35Z and the pod is Running/Ready.

All five nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False and PIDPressure=False; no events were recorded for the otel-demo namespace in the 08:19:31-08:45:16 event window (the only events returned belong to namespace data-recorders).

Span-metric p99 latency between 08:30 and 08:48 stayed in a narrow band for frontend (649-778 ms) and product-catalog (36-61 ms); recommendation p99 rose to 488/744/712 ms at the 08:42-08:45 evaluation points from 154-341 ms earlier in the same window and returned to 139 ms at 08:48, with no accompanying recommendation error burst beyond sporadic flagd EventStream errors.

The alert's firing time is not accompanied by a change in the error signal: the frontend-proxy error counter increased at 0-3 per minute both before and after 08:42:05, and the 3-minute error-span increase oscillates between 0 and 6 spans over 08:22-08:49 without a step change at the alert start.

The 503 UC responses are sporadic terminations of pooled/keep-alive connections between Envoy and the frontend HTTP server (upstream closed the connection before any response bytes), a connection-lifecycle race rather than an application error in frontend; unconfirmed because Jaeger returned no traces for the window and the frontend container produced no readable log lines.

The alert annotation value 0.033333333333333326 equals 2/60, consistent with a per-second error rate of about 2 error spans per minute: the ingress error counter stepped 580->582 between 08:41:27 and 08:43:27 around the 08:42:05 firing. The alert's actual expression cannot be verified because no alerting rules are loaded in this Prometheus.

The much larger early accumulation (at least 557 error spans between the 08:02:12 collector start and 08:15:00, versus about 31 in the following 34 minutes) reflects connection resets during the 08:02 rollout/startup period rather than the condition the 08:42 alert measures.

NetworkPolicy otel-demo/frontend-block-all-ports is not the cause of the frontend-proxy errors: it was created at 08:36:13 (six minutes before the alert) but neither ingress volume (~1,244-1,462 spans/min) nor the error rate changed after its creation, frontend kept serving requests through its single endpoint, and its spec carries only a single empty ingress rule with no from/ports constraints (which the NetworkPolicy API defines as matching all sources on all ports) rather than an empty ingress list.

A frontend application failure is not supported as the cause: the frontend Service emitted zero error spans for every one of its operations, its pod was Ready with restartCount 0 and no previous terminated container, and its CPU (0.048-0.053 cores of a 100m limit) and memory were steady.

The fraud-detection OOMKill is not the cause of the frontend-proxy 503s: it occurred at 08:07:34, before the first observed frontend-proxy error sample, the container restarted successfully at 08:07:35, and the proxy's logged upstream is the frontend Service whose only endpoint is the frontend pod, not fraud-detection.

Verify the RequestErrorRate rule in the alerting backend: with a bare ">0" condition it will keep firing on this ~0.07% steady 503 trickle; a threshold and/or a sustained-duration condition, or excluding 503 UC upstream resets, would match the observed signal.

Review the intent of NetworkPolicy frontend-block-all-ports with its creator: the current manifest (ingress: [{}]) permits all ingress; a deny-all would require an empty ingress list. Change history is not integrated here, so who/what created it at 08:36:13 is unknown.

Inspect the frontend-proxy Envoy upstream connection-pool/idle-timeout and route configuration (baked into image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend-proxy, not in a ConfigMap) together with the frontend Go server's idle/read timeouts, and enable/collect frontend container logs, to confirm why the frontend closes pooled connections.

Reconcile the frontend memory accounting: the container's working set (about 235-246 MiB) reads above the pod's declared 200Mi limit while no OOMKill occurred; check the effective cgroup limit before treating the declared limit as binding.

gaps: Jaeger returned no traces for frontend-proxy or frontend in 08:15-08:49 (traces_search and traces_search_by_tags returned no_data), so no span-level error detail, parent-child call edge or complete trace graph is available for the failing requests.

Pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh produced no readable log lines in 08:15-08:49 (fetch_pod_logs read 0 lines) and has no previous container instance, so the frontend side of the terminated connections could not be read.

frontend-proxy log lines could only be read through about 08:35:18 (4 MiB read limit); later reads for 08:36-08:49 returned no lines, so log-level confirmation of 503s at the 08:42:05 firing time is missing.

No alerting or recording rules are loaded in the queried Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules returned no_data for rule_name RequestErrorRate, for type=alert and unfiltered), so the RequestErrorRate expression, its denominator and its evaluation history are unknown.
Prometheus has no samples before 08:15:00/08:15:05 for these metrics, so there is no pre-incident baseline: whether the 503 trickle existed or was different before 08:15 cannot be determined.
The frontend-proxy Envoy bootstrap/route configuration is not stored in a readable Kubernetes object, so the proxy's upstream connection pool, idle timeout and route timeout settings are unknown.

The change_history integration is not available, so who or what created NetworkPolicy frontend-block-all-ports at 08:36:13 and whether the 08:02 deployment rollout was a scheduled redeploy cannot be determined.

The effective cgroup memory limit for the frontend container could not be read (kube_pod_container_resource_limits returned no_data), so the meaning of the working set exceeding the declared 200Mi limit is unresolved.
next_steps: Confirm the RequestErrorRate rule definition and evaluation window in the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule source that produced this alert.
Compare frontend-proxy Envoy 503 UC timestamps with frontend connection lifecycle settings (idle timeout, max requests per connection) and enable frontend access/error logging.
Decide whether frontend-block-all-ports should be a deny-all policy (empty ingress list) or be removed, and check its change history outside this environment.
Check whether the frontend container's 200Mi memory limit is the effective cgroup limit and whether it should be raised or aligned with the observed working set.
